record.title: Guy's equality conjecture for complete graphs in specified genus ranges
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph, let $S_t$ be the orientable surface of genus $t$, and let $\delta_t(K_n)$ and $\mu_t(K_n)$ denote its Euler excess and skewness, respectively. **Guy's equality conjecture.** If $n=6m$ for $m\geq 1$, then

$$
m-1\leq t\leq 2m^2-3m+1
$$

implies

$$
\delta_t(K_n)=\mu_t(K_n).
$$

The claim is presented as a consequence of a construction based on pair-of-pants cobordisms and handles, and gives equality throughout the stated genus interval for this divisibility class.
record.source_name: Paul C. Kainen, “Skewness, crossing number and Euler's bound for graphs on surfaces”, arXiv:2501.02400 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02400

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2025).

record.title: Weighted-graph third-eigenvalue conjecture
record.statement:
For $n\geq 2$, let $\mathcal{S}_n$ be the set of $n\times n$ real symmetric matrices with entries in $[0,1]$, and let $\lambda_{n-1}(M)$ denote the penultimate eigenvalue of $M$. **Weighted-graph conjecture.** The function $\lambda_{n-1}:\mathcal{S}_n\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfies

$$
-\frac{n}{3} \le \inf_{M\in\mathcal{S}_n}\lambda_{n-1}(M).
$$

This is the weighted-matrix extension of the extremal third-eigenvalue problem; the supplied text presents it as a conjecture and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Giacomo Leonida and Sida Li, “On graphs with large third eigenvalue”, arXiv:2501.02563 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02563

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

record.title: MSO obstruction characterization for bounded linear cliquewidth
record.statement:
Let $\mathscr{C}$ be a class of graphs. A class is **bounded linear cliquewidth** when its linear cliquewidth is bounded, and $\mathsf{CMSO}$ denotes counting monadic second-order logic.

**Linear cliquewidth CMSO obstruction conjecture.** A class of graphs $\mathscr{C}$ has bounded linear cliquewidth if and only if the class of trees cannot be $\mathsf{CMSO}$-transduced from $\mathscr{C}$.

The analogous characterization for cliquewidth is known with the class of all graphs in place of trees, but the linear-cliquewidth version remains open according to the survey.
record.source_name: Michał Pilipczuk, “Graph classes through the lens of logic”, arXiv:2501.04166 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.04166

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2025). “At the point of writing this survey, remains open and presents itself as the main algorithmic goal of the theory under development.”

record.title: Baranyai–Katona wreath conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k\leq n$ be positive integers. Write $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ for the integers modulo $n$, and let $\mathbb{Z}_{n}^{(k)}$ be the set of $k$-element subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$. A **wreath** is a set of the form $\mathcal{F}_{\pi}$ obtained from a permutation $\pi$ of $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ by taking the cyclically indexed blocks of $k$ consecutive values, as defined in the paper.

**The wreath conjecture.** For any positive integers $k\leq n$, there is a decomposition of $\mathbb{Z}_{n}^{(k)}$ into disjoint wreaths.

This conjecture generalizes Baranyai's factorization theorem for complete uniform hypergraphs. It was posed by Baranyai and reformulated in terms of wreaths by Katona; the source does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Jan Petr and Pavel Turek, “Intervals in Dyck paths and the wreath conjecture”, arXiv:2501.07277 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.07277

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

record.title: The AB-graph conjecture for maximal k-covers
record.statement:
Let $S\subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a **$k$-cover**, and suppose that

$$
|S|=2^{n/2}.
$$

An **AB function** is a function $F\colon\mathbb{F}_2^{n/2}\to\mathbb{F}_2^{n/2}$ whose graph is denoted by $\mathcal{G}_F$; two sets are affinely equivalent when they are related by an affine transformation. **AB-graph conjecture.** If $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a $k$-cover with $|S|=2^{n/2}$, then there exists an AB function $F\colon\mathbb{F}_2^{n/2}\to\mathbb{F}_2^{n/2}$ such that $\mathcal{G}_F$ is affinely equivalent to $S$. The theorem preceding the conjecture shows that every such $k$-cover gives a bent function, while graphs of AB functions provide examples; the conjecture asserts that these are the only examples up to affine equivalence.
record.source_name: Darrion Thornburgh, “On generalizing cryptographic results to Sidon sets in F_2^n”, arXiv:2501.11184 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.11184

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

record.title: Submodular-cut extension conjecture for oriented matroids
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be an oriented matroid with underlying matroid, and let $\mathcal{M}$ be a modular cut of that matroid such that there is an extension $\mathcal{O}\cup p$ corresponding to $\mathcal{M}$. Let $\mathcal{M}'\subseteq\mathcal{M}$ also be a modular cut.

**Submodular-cut extension conjecture.** There exists an extension $\mathcal{O}\cup p'$ corresponding to $\mathcal{M}'$.

The authors present this as a potentially useful conjecture for proving the preceding general-rank result and note that it is interesting in its own right. No resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Michael Wilhelmi, “Mutations and (Non-)Euclideaness in oriented matroids”, arXiv:2501.12951 (2025).

record.title: Conjectured Sprague–Grundy values for king moves on generalized staircases with odd equal parameters
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{SG}_{\mathrm{King}}(\mathcal{S}_{r,r}^{k})$ denote the Sprague–Grundy value of the impartial chess game with the king move rule on the generalized staircase determined by parameters $r$, $r$, and $k$. Let $r$ be odd and $k\geq 1$. **The generalized-staircase king conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{SG}_{\mathrm{King}}(\mathcal{S}_{r,r}^{k})=\begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } k\bmod(r+2)\text{ is odd},\\ 1 & \text{if } k\bmod(r+2)\text{ is even and not }0,\\ 2 & \text{if } k\bmod(r+2)=0.\end{cases}
$$

This is posed as an open question about computing Sprague–Grundy values for generalized staircases in impartial chess; the supplied text gives no resolution of this case.
record.source_name: Eric Gottlieb, Matjaž Krnc and Peter Muršič, “Impartial Chess on Integer Partitions”, arXiv:2501.14640 (2025).

record.title: Permutation criterion for two families of pentanomials over finite fields
record.statement:
Let $m$ and $k$ be positive integers and set $q=2^m$. Define

$$
f_1(x)=x^{2^k+1}+x^{2^kq^2+1}+x^{q+2^k}+x^{q^2+2^k}+x^{2^kq+1}
$$

and

$$
f_2(x)=x^{2^k+1}+x^{(2^k+1)q}+x^{q+2^k}+x^{q^2+2^k}+x^{2^kq^2+q}.
$$

**Permutation criterion.** The polynomials $f_1$ and $f_2$ are permutation polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_{q^3}$ if and only if

$$
\operatorname{gcd}(2^k+1,q-1)=1.
$$

This conjecture is based on numerical results concerning permutation pentanomials over finite fields of characteristic two; the supplied text does not establish whether the criterion has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Tongliang Zhang, Lijing Zheng, Hengtai Wang, Jie Peng and Yanjun Li, “Further results on permutation pentanomials over F_q^3 in characteristic two”, arXiv:2501.15741 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15741

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

record.title: Kruft's terminal-set conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a **terminal set** if $S$ is a general position set of $G$ and adding any vertex $u\in V(G)-S$ to $S$ creates three-in-a-line with $u$ as an endpoint. **Kruft's conjecture.** Every graph has a terminal set.

Terminal sets correspond to maximal general position sets contained in a layer of a Cartesian product. The conjecture is known for graphs of diameter at most three, cographs, and chordal graphs, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Ullas Chandran S. V., Sandi Klavžar and James Tuite, “The General Position Problem: A Survey”, arXiv:2501.19385 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19385

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2025). “Another open problem is given in the following conjectured Nordhaus-Gaddum relation.”

record.title: Strong contextuality conjecture for universally transversal code-switching protocols
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{Q}_1$ and $\mathcal{Q}_2$ be subsystem stabilizer codes, and consider a fault-tolerant code-switching protocol between them. Let the **set of transversal gates** for each code be the gates implementable transversally on that code. **Strong contextuality conjecture.** If the union of the set of transversal gates for $\mathcal{Q}_1$ and that for $\mathcal{Q}_2$ forms a universal gate set, then the code-switching protocol must be strongly contextual in a partial closure. This is proposed as a no-go principle for noncontextual routes to transversal universality through code-switching; the supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Derek Khu, Andrew Tanggara, Chao Jin and Kishor Bharti, “Contextuality of Quantum Error-Correcting Codes”, arXiv:2502.02553 (2026).

record.title: Binary deleted-subspace basis conjecture
record.statement:
Let $r$ and $c$ be integers with $1\le c\le r-1$. For a subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^r$, call a basis an $r$-element linearly independent subset.

**Binary Bose–Burton basis conjecture.** Among all subsets of $\mathbb{F}_2^r$ of size $2^r-2^{r-c}$, the one with the most bases is obtained by deleting a copy of the subspace $\mathbb{F}_2^{r-c}$ from $\mathbb{F}_2^r$.

This is stated as the binary equivalent of the preceding Bose–Burton conjecture. The source gives no further resolution beyond the cases $t=2$ and $r\le3$ for the equivalent formulation.

record.title: Bensmail–Filasto–Hocquard–Marcille conjecture on mixed local irregularity
record.statement:
A sink-source path is an oriented path containing an arc directed into a vertex and an arc directed out of that vertex, as used in the source. For $a,b\in\{+,-\}$, define $(a,b)$-local irregularity by requiring $d^a(u)\neq d^b(v)$ on every arc $uv$, and let $\mathrm{lir}^{(+,-)}(D)$ be the corresponding chromatic index. **Bensmail–Filasto–Hocquard–Marcille conjecture.** Every digraph $D$ without a sink-source path satisfies

$$
\mathrm{lir}^{(+,-)}(D)\leq 3.
$$

The source gives a constant upper bound of seven for digraphs without a sink-source path, but does not report that the conjectured bound three has been attained.
record.source_name: Igor Grzelec, Alfréd Onderko and Mariusz Woźniak, “Weak and strong local irregularity of digraphs”, arXiv:2502.07933 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07933

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2025). “During their research, a single counterexample to the Local Irregularity Conjecture was found in .”

record.title: Häggkvist's avoidability conjecture for $(m,m,m)$-arrays
record.statement: An $(m,m,m)$-array is an $n\times n$ array of sets of size at most $m$, such that each number in $[n]$ occurs at most $m$ times among the sets in any row or column. It is **avoidable** if there exists an $n\times n$ Latin square $L$ such that no entry of $L$ is contained in the set in the corresponding cell of the array. **Häggkvist's avoidability conjecture.** There exists a constant $\gamma>0$ such that if $m<\gamma n$, then every $(m,m,m)$-array is avoidable. This conjecture asks for a uniform linear range in which all such arrays admit an avoiding Latin square; the source gives no resolution here.
record.source_name: Candida Bowtell, Alice Devillers, André Kündgen, Padraig Ó Catháin and Ian M. Wanless, “Extendibility of Latin Hypercuboids”, arXiv:2502.08868 (2025).

record.title: Positivity conjecture for permanents of polystochastic matrices
record.statement:
A $d$-dimensional polystochastic matrix of order $n$ is a nonnegative array whose sums over every line are equal to $1$. Its permanent is

$$
\operatorname{per} A=\sum_{\ell\in D(A)}\prod_{\alpha\in\ell}a_{\alpha},
$$

where $D(A)$ is the set of diagonals of $A$, and a diagonal is a collection of $n$ indices such that no two share the same hyperplane. **Positivity conjecture.** Every polystochastic matrix of even dimension or odd order has a positive permanent. For odd dimension at least $3$ and even order, examples of polystochastic matrices with zero permanent are known, while no such matrices are known for the remaining parameter values; the conjecture asserts positivity in those remaining cases.
record.source_name: Anna A. Taranenko, “Enumeration and constructions of vertices of the polytope of polystochastic matrices”, arXiv:2502.09149 (2025).

record.title: Linear-forest conjecture for chords of longest cycles
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-connected graph with $k\ge 2$, and let $F$ be a **linear forest**, meaning a subgraph whose components are possibly empty paths. Suppose that $F$ has $l$ edges and $t$ isolated vertices, with

$$
l+t\le k-2.
$$

A cycle passes through $F$ when it passes through $E(F)\cup V(F)$.

**Linear-forest chord conjecture.** Every longest cycle of $G$ passing through $F$ has a chord.

This is proposed as a generalization of the paper's main conjectures. The cited preceding result gives a lower bound for the length of a cycle passing through $F$, but the supplied text does not establish the chord assertion.
record.source_name: Haidong Wu and Shunzhe Zhang, “Chords of longest cycles passing through a specified small set”, arXiv:2502.10657 (2025).

record.title: The double Hall path-cover conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=(X,Y)$ be a dHp bigraph. Write $\mathsf{\Lambda}_G(X)$ for the neighborhood of $X$ in $Y$, and let a **$Y$-$Y$ path** be a path whose two endpoints lie in $Y$.

**Double Hall path-cover conjecture.** If

$$
|\mathsf{\Lambda}_G(X)|\geq |X|+1,
$$

then there exists a collection of disjoint $Y$-$Y$ paths whose union covers all of $X$.

The paper presents this as a conjecture weaker than Salia's cycle conjecture and proves that it is equivalent to another such weakening. Its general status is open.
record.source_name: Guantao Chen, Mikhail Lavrov, Yuying Ma, Yimo Su and Jennifer Vandenbussche, “Bipartite graphs with the double Hall property”, arXiv:2502.10903 (2025).

record.title: Ryser's maximum permanent conjecture for regular (0,1)-matrices
record.statement:
Let $\mathscr{U}(v,k)$ be the set of all $(0,1)$-matrices of order $v$ with exactly $k$ 1's in each row and column. Let $J$ be the all-1 matrix of order $k$, and suppose that $k$ divides $v$. Let $J^*$ be the direct sum of $v/k$ copies of $J$. Then $J^*\in\mathscr{U}(v,k)$.

**Ryser's conjecture.** The permanent of $J^*$ is maximal in $\mathscr{U}(v,k)$.

This is a classical extremal problem for permanents of regular $(0,1)$-matrices. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
record.source_name: Tingzeng Wu, Xiangshuai Dong and Huazhong Lü, “Brualdi-Goldwasser-Michael problem for maximum permanents of (0,1)-matrices”, arXiv:2502.12787 (2025).

record.title: Expansion conjecture for joint-ancestor-free subsets
record.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a formal Markov chain, and let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be connected components of the cut graph $C_1(G)$. Let $I\subseteq K_1$ and $J\subseteq K_2$ be joint-ancestor-free subsets, with at least one inclusion strict. **Expansion conjecture.** There exists either an element $i\in K_1\setminus I$ such that $I\cup\{i\}$ and $J$ are joint-ancestor free, or an element $j\in K_2\setminus J$ such that $I$ and $J\cup\{j\}$ are joint-ancestor free. This conjecture is proposed as an approach toward proving the equivalence of broad and narrow second-level cuts, but the source leaves it open.
record.source_name: Céline Comte and Isaac Grosof, “Graph-Based Product Form”, arXiv:2502.13890 (2025).

record.title: Forest sufficient condition for polynomial approximation homomorphism complexity
record.statement:
Let $F$ and $H$ be graphs. Let an **$F$-forest** $T$ be the forest construction used in the source, and let $T^{\star}$ denote its associated graph. **Forest sufficient-condition conjecture.** If there exists an $F$-forest $T$ such that 
$$
T\rightarrow F\qquad\text{and}\qquad H\rightarrow T^{\star},
$$
 then 
$$
M_{F,H}(\varepsilon)=\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon).
$$
 This is presented immediately after the conjectural characterisation of polynomial versus exponential behaviour and is intended as the polynomial side of that dichotomy. The supplied text does not establish this statement as a theorem, and the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Lior Gishboliner, Eoin Hurley and Yuval Wigderson, “Asymmetric results about graph homomorphisms”, arXiv:2502.20278 (2026).

record.title: The bowtie three-in-or-three-out conjecture
record.statement:
Let $B=F_{2,3}$ be the bowtie graph, with a distinguished center vertex, and let $\vec{B}$ be an orientation of $B$ having exactly three edges directed toward the center vertex or exactly three edges directed away from it. **The bowtie three-in-or-three-out conjecture.** Then 
$$
D(n,\vec{B})=2^{\mathrm{ex}(n,B)}.
$$
 This is the remaining unresolved orientation case after the other bowtie orientations were shown to have more than $2^{\mathrm{ex}(n,B)}$ orientations; whether the displayed equality holds remains open.
